content:
Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. As a data scientist with over four years of experience in a subscription business, I have built forecasting and customer models and delivered scheduled scoring workflows. I would welcome the opportunity to develop my production engineering skills while helping your team build tools for merchants and support agents.

At Thistlebox, I built a LightGBM recipe-demand forecasting model using calendar, price and menu-position features. It runs as a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook, writing results to BigQuery for operations teams. The model reduced forecast error from 23% to 14% and food waste by an estimated 9%. I have also added pytest unit tests for its feature code and built an XGBoost churn model scored weekly in BigQuery.

Alongside modelling, I write production SQL, maintain dbt models and work with product and growth colleagues on experimentation. I built a Python and Streamlit testing calculator used by approximately 25 colleagues and wrote its Dockerfile; our data platform team handles its deployment. Presenting results to leadership and delivering internal statistics training have helped me communicate technical work to different audiences.

My MSc in Statistics gave me a strong foundation in modelling and evaluation. I would be glad to bring that background, my Python experience and a practical approach to Quillstone’s collaborative AI team. Thank you for considering my application; I would welcome the chance to discuss the role with you.

Kind regards,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, honest, and appropriately concise. It uses credible quantified evidence, including the forecasting improvement, food-waste reduction, testing-calculator adoption, and testing activity. The progression from modelling to production-oriented work is understandable. However, it is only moderately targeted to Customer Support AI: it does not connect the candidate’s experience to support operations, merchant problems, AI products, data pipelines, or the company’s ownership and teamwork culture. The closing is also somewhat generic and could make a more specific case for the transition from data science to machine learning engineering.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is highly parseable: it uses standard headings-free prose, conventional paragraphs, and no problematic tables, graphics, or unusual formatting. It includes useful keywords such as Python, LightGBM, XGBoost, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, pytest, dbt, Docker, SQL, and A/B testing. The AI screening probability is moderate rather than high because several job-ad terms supported by the candidate’s material are absent or insufficiently explicit, especially GCP, feature engineering, data pipelines, orchestration, automated tests, and production ML systems. The letter should use the exact supported terms rather than relying on an ATS to infer them from product names. It must not add unsupported terms such as RAG, chat assistants, MLflow, Airflow, model APIs, monitoring, or data versioning.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document demonstrates relevant transferable experience: more than four years as a data scientist, production-oriented batch and scheduled ML workflows, Python modelling, feature use, BigQuery/dbt data work, cloud-based tooling, and automated tests. It also credibly explains the candidate’s interest in developing further production engineering skills. The main alignment limitations are substantive candidate gaps rather than writing defects: the candidate has not worked four years as a machine learning engineer, has no chat-assistant or RAG experience, has not independently deployed a model API, and has no stated experience with monitoring, data versioning, MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow, or equivalent MLOps tooling. The letter also does not currently reflect Quillstone’s emphasis on ownership, teamwork, pragmatic problem-solving, learning from mistakes, or sharing context openly. These gaps should not be disguised, but the letter can make the strongest truthful case through transferable experience and explicit motivation.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the second paragraph, revise the forecasting example to include the job’s supported terminology: change the sentence beginning "At Thistlebox, I built a LightGBM..." to explain that you engineered calendar, price, and menu-position features and delivered a scheduled batch scoring workflow in Vertex AI Workbench that wrote predictions to BigQuery for operational use. For example: "At Thistlebox, I engineered calendar, price and menu-position features for a LightGBM demand-forecasting model and delivered a scheduled batch scoring workflow in Vertex AI Workbench that writes predictions to BigQuery for operational use." This makes feature engineering, cloud, data pipeline, and production workflow experience explicit without implying API serving.
2. In the paragraph beginning "Alongside modelling," explicitly name the supported engineering practices and orchestration experience. Add that you maintain dbt data models and use scheduled notebook jobs and dbt Cloud scheduling for recurring data and scoring workflows, if the latter is accurate as stated in the candidate information. Also retain the existing pytest evidence. Do not describe this as MLflow, Airflow, Kubernetes, monitoring, model serving, or full MLOps if those claims are not supported.
3. In the opening paragraph, make the transition and role fit more specific. Replace "I would welcome the opportunity to develop my production engineering skills while helping your team build tools for merchants and support agents" with wording that connects existing experience to the role, such as: "I am now moving from data science toward machine learning engineering, bringing experience building and operating scheduled ML workflows, and I am motivated to apply that foundation to practical AI tools that help merchants and support teams." This remains truthful while aligning with the Customer Support AI context.
4. Before the closing paragraph, add one concise culture-alignment sentence grounded in the documented experience: mention collaborating with product and growth colleagues, presenting results to leadership, and delivering "Stats for PMs" training. For example: "My work with product and growth teams, leadership presentations, and internal Stats for PMs training has taught me to share context clearly, work collaboratively, and turn technical results into practical decisions." This supports Quillstone’s teamwork, context-sharing, and learning signals without claiming experience the candidate has not provided.
5. In the final paragraph, explicitly name GCP rather than only naming individual services. For example, change "my Python experience" to "my Python experience and hands-on use of GCP services including BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench." Keep the wording at the level of hands-on service use; do not imply broad GCP infrastructure expertise.
6. Do not add claims about chat assistants, RAG, language-model fine-tuning, model APIs, monitoring, data versioning, MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow, Kubernetes, or independent Cloud Run deployment. The current letter is appropriately honest about the data platform team handling deployment, and preserving that accuracy is essential.

content:
Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. As a data scientist with over four years of experience in a subscription business, I have built forecasting and customer models and delivered scheduled scoring workflows. I am now moving from data science toward machine learning engineering, bringing experience building and operating scheduled ML workflows, and I am motivated to apply that foundation to practical AI tools that help merchants and support teams.

At Thistlebox, I engineered calendar, price and menu-position features for a LightGBM demand-forecasting model and delivered a scheduled batch scoring workflow in Vertex AI Workbench that writes predictions to BigQuery for operational use. It runs as a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook, writing results to BigQuery for operations teams. The model reduced forecast error from 23% to 14% and food waste by an estimated 9%. I have also added pytest unit tests for its feature code and built an XGBoost churn model scored weekly in BigQuery.

Alongside modelling, I write production SQL, maintain dbt data models, use dbt Cloud scheduling for recurring data workflows and scheduled notebook jobs for scoring, and work with product and growth colleagues on experimentation. I built a Python and Streamlit testing calculator used by approximately 25 colleagues and wrote its Dockerfile; our data platform team handles its deployment. Presenting results to leadership and delivering internal statistics training have helped me communicate technical work to different audiences.

My work with product and growth teams, leadership presentations, and internal Stats for PMs training has taught me to share context clearly, work collaboratively, and turn technical results into practical decisions.

My MSc in Statistics gave me a strong foundation in modelling and evaluation. I would be glad to bring that background, my Python experience and hands-on use of GCP services including BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench, and a practical approach to Quillstone’s collaborative AI team. Thank you for considering my application; I would welcome the chance to discuss the role with you.

Kind regards,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is professional, truthful, and supported by the candidate information. It presents relevant evidence: feature engineering, scheduled batch scoring, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt, automated tests, Docker, experimentation, and communication with stakeholders. The quantified forecasting results strengthen credibility. However, the second paragraph repeats the same Vertex AI Workbench and BigQuery workflow twice, making the letter less concise. The letter also spends substantial space restating technical details without clearly distinguishing the candidate’s current production experience from the more advanced requirements of the target Machine Learning Engineer role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses ATS-friendly plain text formatting, standard section-free letter structure, and relevant keywords including Python, GCP, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, feature engineering, automated tests, Docker, dbt, scheduled workflows, and production SQL. AI screening probability is moderate: the document contains several relevant keywords, but does not contain supported evidence for model serving, monitoring, data versioning, language models, chat assistants, RAG, or named MLOps tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow, or Airflow. These are genuine experience gaps rather than terms that should be added without evidence.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with Python-based modelling, feature engineering, cloud data workflows, scheduled batch scoring, experimentation, automated testing, and practical collaboration with product and growth teams. The candidate’s MSc Statistics is relevant to modelling and evaluation, but the advertised degree preference is machine learning, computer science, or a related engineering field. The candidate has over four years as a data scientist, not four years as a machine learning engineer shipping ML systems to production. The candidate also lacks documented experience with customer-support AI products, chat assistants or RAG, large text datasets, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, and formal MLOps platforms. The letter appropriately avoids claiming these capabilities. References to leadership communication, internal training, and practical decision-making support Quillstone’s teamwork, shared context, and learning culture, although the culture alignment could be made more specific without overstating it.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the second paragraph, remove the duplicated sentence beginning "It runs as a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook..." because the preceding sentence already states that the workflow runs in Vertex AI Workbench and writes predictions to BigQuery. Keep the more complete version and retain the quantified WAPE and food-waste results.

MINOR — In the third paragraph, replace the wording "use dbt Cloud scheduling for recurring data workflows and scheduled notebook jobs for scoring" with a more precise description such as "use dbt Cloud scheduling for recurring data workflows and scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook jobs for batch scoring." This makes the orchestration and batch nature of the work clearer without implying model serving or broader MLOps ownership.

MINOR — In the fourth paragraph, consolidate the repeated references to product and growth teams, leadership presentations, and "Stats for PMs" training. For example, replace that paragraph with: "Working with product and growth teams, presenting results to leadership, and delivering three internal Stats for PMs sessions have strengthened my ability to share context clearly, collaborate across functions, and turn technical results into practical decisions."
